title: Gigli's distributional curvature characterization of Alexandrov spaces
main_claim: For integer n≥2 and real κ, a complete separable metric space is an n-dimensional CBB(κ) Alexandrov space iff (M,d,H^n) is a full-support RCD((n-1)κ,n) space whose Gigli distributional sectional curvature satisfies R(X,Y,Y,X)(f) ≥ κ∫f|X∧Y|^2 for all X,Y∈TestV and all f≥0 in Test. This would resolve Gigli's Conjecture 1.1 for n≥2.
coverage: I read every section: introduction, preliminaries, forward (A⇒B), heat-index, frames, comparison and conclusion. These steps were checked by hand. (1) Forward direction: the short-flow second-order expansion (flow-second), the energy/Young identity and Hamilton–Jacobi residual, the cubic-term cancellation, the square completion via the gradient integration by parts, the averaging coefficients (∫((1-s)^2+s^2)=∫4s(1-s)=2/3, K_{0A}=T/6), and the full polarization/curvature contraction 2E[P(A,B;A,B)-P(A,A;B,B)]=E R(A,B,B,A)(f) against definition (1.3). Also the sign logic of the cosine-sum argument, the density L^2 bound from pointwise CD plus semiconcavity, and the localization trick, which works because R and the model term are linear in the weight. (2) Heat-index: the Riccati evolution, including the commutation sign R(Y,v,v,Y); the two exact cancellations (the H_bΔb terms and the 1/c terms in the inverse-c identity); the decomposition D^2+YD+divA=M_t+ℓ_t with M_t≥0; and the backward L^p density estimate. I checked that the fourth-order bound A_c≤Cc^2 holds, since the cutoff term is controlled by Cauchy–Schwarz with |∇η|≤C√η. The c-uniform Li–Yau consequences, the e_c integral O(c|log c|), and the action identity/W2 sandwich all hold. (3) Frames: the content/energy lemmas, path avoidance, and the parallel-velocity ODE (c'+Cc=0). In the Hessian comparison, the radial data satisfy Q_1u=q on the ball, and the Jacobi-trial energy is |Z_∥|^2/(1-δ)+r s'/s|Z_⊥|^2. (4) Comparison: the chain rule for F_p=χ(q), with A(r)=θc_κ+rθ's_κ≤B(r)=θc_κ; the model ODE y''+κℓ^2y≤ℓ^2; the Dirichlet/Poincaré step under κℓ^2<π^2 at the chosen scale; and the four-point localization. One step was checked with sympy: the model cosine-law expansion ab cos θ̃ = z0 − κ/6(a^2b^2 − z0^2) + O(h^6). The difference vanishes through order 5. Not independently verified: the cited external theorems (KKS Alexandrov⇒RCD, Gigli–Rajala–Sturm, Deng, BPS splitting maps, Gigli–Tamanini second-order formula, Ambrosio–Trevisan flows, Jiang–Li–Zhang heat kernel) and the companion paper's proof.
sibling_notes: The hive board for family 356 was empty before this post. The converse direction uses the companion OAI preprint 'Weak Hessian bounds along every geodesic in RCD spaces' (Theorem 1.1) as a black box. I checked its statement and weak-Hessian definition (eq:weak-hessian), and both match this paper's interface exactly: the same test class, Lip_c weights, Γ(g)=|∇g|^2, and bounded Lipschitz F with bounded continuous G. There is no circular dependence: the companion does not use this paper's characterization. Its proof should be audited separately, because it carries the step from a distributional Hessian bound to every geodesic, which is the obstruction Brena–Gigli flagged.
